fact: The DGDDL handed the commune of Assinie-Mafia a USB key with its taxpayer database on 9 December 2025, within the PAMREC pilot project; no count of communes recording is given.
The DGDDL, the Directorate General of Decentralisation and Local Development, ran the handover of taxpayer databases under the PAMREC pilot.
The SYGIDAN-RECETTES tool was to be proven by 31 December 2024 and, in the PAMREC pilot phase, deployed to 22 communes; the DGDDL director said it would then be distributed to all from January 2025.

The DGDDL director described SYGIDAN-RECETTES as digitalising all of a commune's revenues, with traceability each time a tax is collected, and centralising data from all revenue actors; it was at pre-validation.
The tool is to centralise the data coming from all actors collecting local revenue, to be implemented in all collectivities; it was still at pre-validation.
The software was developed by the DGDDL's own services, which is also PAMREC's national project directorate.
PAMREC was financed by the African Development Bank and the Ivorian State, together 3,003,901,293 FCFA.
The PAMREC pilot phase of about 20 months was to deploy the PROTON tax system in 19 municipalities; launch ceremony 27 July 2023.
PROTON is described as centralising geo-referenced taxpayer data and their payments, with collectors on mobile devices; planned for the pilot, not stated as live.
The Revenue Development Foundation, technical partner, developed PROTON and deploys it with the DGDDL.
PAMREC is funded through a partnership between the Republic of Côte d'Ivoire and the African Development Bank; no split is given.

The Treasury study (cover dated September 2018) reports that local collection mostly proceeds by public-accountant-appointed revenue collectors before orders are issued, with receipt books; collectors keep parallel receipt books, and the study recommends secure printed receipt books.
The Treasury study states that local governments lack reliable databases of the taxpayers liable to local taxes, and recommends a census of taxpayers to build a computer database.
Net Collect Services, a Treasury-backed collection software, was in trial in some communes including Grand-Bassam and Bingerville, out of 201 communes in May 2018; the study urges deployment to all.
The Treasury (Direction générale du Trésor et de la Comptabilité publique) decided to accompany automation of local collection with the Net Collect Services software.

The AfDB appraisal (July 2021) places the PAMREC pilot in 22 municipalities out of 201, January 2021 to June 2024, to digitise local tax collection and the taxpayer registration system; the Government intends to extend it to all municipalities and districts later.

The system to be deployed registers taxpayers and records collection of fees, payments and revenue, with balances, arrears and penalties, syncing field data from mobile devices; planned, not yet live at appraisal.

The appraisal states current local tax collection mechanisms are obsolete and inefficient, and sets the baseline at 0% of collection operations on fully digital support and 0 new taxpayers in a database.

The project is to centralise municipal data and connect the system to those of the tax directorate (DGI), the Treasury (DGTCP), DGDDL or the Court of Auditors; the target is integration with at least one, from a baseline of none.

The Ministry of Interior and Security, through the DGDDL, is executing agency and project unit; the Revenue Development Foundation is technical partner under a 2018 memorandum, and the system carries no licence fees.
A costed project plan names the system: CFAF 3,003,901,293 over January 2021 to June 2024, with a results framework and a 100% target for revenue staff trained.
Financing is an African Development Fund loan of UA 3 million (78%) with a Government of Côte d'Ivoire counterpart of UA 0.86 million (22%), mobilisable from 2022.
A Net Collect Service run by Business Management Invest Côte d'Ivoire (BMI-CI) was piloted in 2017 in more than twenty municipalities; the appraisal says municipalities were reluctant over its cost.
The Net Collect Service operator is paid 9% of the revenue collected, which the appraisal gives as a reason it was rejected for PAMREC.
